answer.why: Both companies are vertically integrated civil infrastructure contractors that produce hot-mix asphalt and mine/process aggregates, win work through competitive public bidding, and serve state/local transportation agencies. That core overlap is very strong. However, Granite explicitly positions itself as a "full-suite provider in the transportation, water infrastructure and mineral exploration markets" [T:P1.4, T:P2.3], making water/wastewater infrastructure a named, material market. CPI describes itself as "A Leading Asphalt-Centered Infrastructure Company" [C:P1.4] whose "focus" is "constructing, repairing, and maintaining surface infrastructure" [C:P1.2, C:P1.5]—there is no evidence CPI serves water infrastructure. Under the several-businesses rule, a comp that matches only one of the target's material businesses is capped at 1. CPI is a strong match on the transportation/road-paving business but does not cover Granite's water infrastructure market, so the grade is 1 (adjacent_peer).

C:P1.1.text: Construction Partners Inc. | Building Connected Communities

C:P1.6.text: Asphalt Solutions for the Road Ahead

C:P1.7.text: Construction Partners operates a network of asphalt plants, construction teams, liquid asphalt terminals, and aggregate facilities that work together to support its projects and customers.
